title: Telemetry Compaction and Retention Tuning Playbook
author: Sofia Alvarez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the operational process, decision criteria, dashboards, and runbook steps for compaction and retention tuning across Redwood's telemetry pipelines. The goal is to reduce storage and query costs while preserving signals required for SLOs, incident triage, and ML-driven automation.

Scope: applies to high-volume operational telemetry streams that feed long-term storage, analytics indices, and derived SLI backfills (examples: token-cost, request-latency, kv-cache-metrics, model-variant-switches). Does NOT cover audit logs (handled under security-and-compliance) or raw customer PII telemetry (special retention rules).

Owner and stakeholders
- Playbook owner: Observability Platform (eng-platform)
- Primary operator: Platform Operators (oncall)
- Stakeholders: Serving Runtime, SRE, Cost Engineering, Product Analytics

Signals and SLOs to protect
- Tokenized SLI preservation: 99.9% availability of token-cost time-series at 1-minute granularity for last 30 days
- Incident forensic window: ability to reconstruct request traces for any production incident for last 90 days (aggregate level acceptable)
- Cost target: reduce long-term storage growth rate for telemetry indices by 35% in 90 days after tuning

Retention tiers and compaction rules (recommended defaults)
- Hot tier (0-7 days): full fidelity, 1m aggregation for metrics, full traces (sampled at configured rate)
- Warm tier (8-30 days): metrics aggregated to 5m, traces kept as index pointers (no raw spans), event logs compressed with delta-encoding
- Cold tier (31-180 days): metrics aggregated to 60m, top-K anomaly windows preserved at 1m for top 1% of active services, traces evicted except for anchor events (errors, model-fallbacks)
- Archive tier (>180 days): compressed deltas and sparse index for compliance queries (retention schedules controlled by legal)

Compaction matrix (example)
| Signal category | Hot -> Warm | Warm -> Cold | Cold -> Archive | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Token-cost (per-tenant) | 1m -> 5m aggregate | 5m -> 60m rollup | compress + sparse index | Keep top 10 tenants fully for 90d |
| Request latency (p50/p95/p99) | full 1m series | 5m series, store p50/p95 only | 60m p95 and counts | Retain histograms for 30d |
| KV prefix cache metrics | 1m series + shards | 5m rollup | 60m rollup with hotspot markers | Preserve rebalancing events |
| Traces/spans | sampled raw traces (1%) | keep span pointers + error traces | drop raw spans except anchors | Increase sampling on degradation |

Dashboards and alerting to implement before tuning
1) Retention Health dashboard (owner: Observability Platform)
   - Inputs: per-index retention size, ingest rate, compaction job success/failure, read query latency
   - Visuals: stacked retention by tier, weekly growth trend, compaction lag (s)
2) Forensics Coverage dashboard (owner: SRE)
   - Inputs: trace sampling rate, percent of incidents with reconstructable traces, top missing-services
   - Visuals: heatmap of services by trace coverage and error rate
3) Cost vs Coverage tradeoff dashboard (owner: Cost Eng)
   - Inputs: storage cost delta pre/post compaction, SLO hit-rate changes, query latency 95p

Alert thresholds
- Compaction job failure: any job fails 1x -> P1 pager to Observability Platform
- Compaction lag > 2x configured window (e.g., 48h lag for nightly rollups) -> P2 notification
- Forensics coverage drop: reconstructable incidents < 95% for past 7 days -> P1 escalation to SRE and Serving Runtime

Preflight checklist (run this before any global retention change)
- [ ] Stakeholder signoff (SRE, Cost Eng, Security)
- [ ] Backstop snapshot: take a metadata snapshot of all indices (index mappings, sizes, retention settings)
- Command: curl -s -u $OBS_USER:$(cat /secrets/obs_token) https://es.internal/_cat/indices?v > /tmp/indices-snapshot.json
- [ ] Run compaction canary against a non-critical tenant for 7 days
- [ ] Ensure synthetic rollback job is ready (to restore last 7d raw data from hot replicas for selected tenants)

Step-by-step tuning runbook
1) Confirm baseline
   - Collect 14-day baseline: ingest rate, storage growth, top-50 services by telemetry volume, average query latency (90p).
   - Run: internal tooling `telemetry-metrics baseline --window 14d --out ./baseline.json`
2) Configure compaction policy in index template
   - Example template snippet (YAML style):
     index_patterns: ["telemetry-*token-cost*"]
     settings:
       number_of_shards: 1
       lifecycle:
         name: telemetry-lifecycle
         phases:
           hot:
             min_age: 0d
             actions: { rollover: { max_size: "50gb", max_age: "7d" } }
           warm:
             min_age: 7d
             actions: { forcemerge: { max_num_segments: 1 }, shrink: { number_of_shards: 1 } }
           cold:
             min_age: 30d
             actions: { freeze: {} }
3) Apply compaction to canary tenant(s)
   - Select canaries: 3 tenants covering different profiles (spiky, steady, high-variance)
   - Monitor Retention Health and Forensics Coverage daily for 7 days
4) Evaluate impact and iterate
   - Use Cost vs Coverage dashboard: if storage reduction < target or coverage drop > 2%, rollback changes for that tenant and increase warm retention window
5) Gradual rollout
   - 10% tenants -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% by volume, wait 7 days between steps and run verification suite each time
6) Post-rollout verification
   - Confirm compaction job success for all indices, query latency at baseline +/- 10%, forensics reconstructable incidents >= 99% for 30 days

Rollback and emergency recovery
- If a P1 triggers (coverage loss, critical query failures):
  1) Pause new compaction jobs globally: `observabilityctl compaction pause --all`
  2) Restore hot replicas for affected indices from snapshot: `es-snapshot-restore --index telemetry-token-cost-2026.01 --target hot-replica`
  3) Notify stakeholders and open incident with runbook link

Operational automation recipes
- Auto-scale compaction workers based on backlog: policy uses backlog-ms > 300000 -> scale +50%
- Adaptive sampling toggle: when p95 latency > service-specific threshold AND error rate up 2x -> double trace sampling for 12h for affected service
- Scheduled re-evaluation job: monthly job that computes ROI of retention settings and suggests adjustments; outputs review PR to Cost Eng

Telemetry queries and CLI examples
- Check index sizes by tier: `es-query --indices 'telemetry-*' --fields index,store.size_in_bytes,creation.date`
- Compaction job status: `observabilityctl compaction status --since 7d`
- Reconstruct sample trace for tenant T: `trace-extract --tenant T --time '2026-02-20T03:00:00Z' --out trace.json`

Postmortem and retrospective template (required after any P1)
1) Summary (1-2 sentences)
2) Timeline with timestamps
3) Root cause and contributing factors
4) Metrics impact (storage, cost, SLI delta)
5) Action items (owner, due date)
6) Follow-ups (policy adjustments, dashboard additions)

Run cadence and ownership
- Quarterly retention review (owner: Observability Platform)
- Monthly ROI job (owner: Cost Eng)
- Oncall playbook review annually (owner: SRE)

Appendix: decision heuristics quick reference
- If a signal is critical to P1 investigation -> retain 1m fidelity for 90d
- If a signal is used only for weekly trends -> prefer 1h compaction starting at 30d
- Preserve raw traces for services that show >2x median error spikes month-over-month

References and links
- Elastic lifecycle docs: internal link to canonical templates
- Cost playbook for telemetry: see Cost Eng page (related_pages)
